raw_characteristics_excerpt: Study characteristics Methods Study design: randomised controlled trial Study grouping: parallel group Participants Baseline Characteristics Megestrol •Age (mean ± standard deviation): 34 ± 7.1 Metformin and megestrol •Age (mean ± standard deviation): 36.4 ± 4.2 Included criteria: pathologically diagnosed with EAH, aged 45 years or less, desire to preserve fertility and at least one sign of metabolic syndrome Excluded criteria: alcoholism, pregnancy, severe infection, complicated clinical diseases (heart, liv- er, lung and kidney dysfunction), severe cardiovascular disease, allergy to MA or metformin, thrombo- sis, breast cancer history, other reproductive system malignancies (including EC), contraindications for treatment of either MA or metformin and previous hormonal treatment Pretreatment: the mean ages of the MA and MET group participants were 34 ± 7.1 and 36.4 ± 4.2 years, respectively. There was no statistically significant difference in age distribution between the two groups (P = 0.433). All participants were married, and 37.5% of the participants (6/16) had a history of infertility. Furthermore, 50% of the participants (8/16) met the MS criteria, and 50% of the participants (4/8) had MS in both the MA and MET groups. raw_characteristics_excerpt: Study characteristics Methods Study design •Prospective, open-label RCT •Duration of study/recruitment dates: August 2014 and July 2015 •Duration of follow-up: 7 days •Setting: multicentre (5 academic medical centres) •Country: Korea Participants Study characteristics •Inclusion criteria: women ≥ 18 years with pyuria that was confirmed by a urinalysis that showed more than 5 WBC/hpf; complained of more than 2 symptoms, including urination frequency, dysuria, ur- gency, and lower abdominal discomfort. •Exclusion criteria: interstitial cystitis, a history of cystitis within 2 weeks, suspected febrile UTI, and bladder outlet obstruction (residual urine > 100 mL); taking antibiotics or analgesics due to other med- ical conditions Baseline characteristics •Number: intervention group (28); control group (27) •Mean age ± SD (years): intervention group (50.26 ± 14.8); control group (49.61 ± 12.3) •Number with previous UTIs (last 5 years): cystitis more than once (68%), more than twice (34%), and more than 5 times (5%); data stratified by treatment group not reported Interventions Intervention group (NSAIDs + antibiotic) •Aceclofenac: 100 mg, twice /day for 3 days •Cefpodoxime: 100 mg, twice/day for 3 days Control group (antibiotic) •Cefpodoxime: 100 mg, twice /day for 3 days Outcomes Reported outcomes •Difference in severity of dysuria reported on a numerical pain scale after each treatment Notes Additional informationKo 2018 Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for treating symptomatic uncomplicated urinary tract infections in non-pregnant adult women (Review) Copyright © 2024 The Cochrane Collaboration.
